problem:
Scientists are observing a colony of bugs. The population $P(t)$ of the colony is given by the function

$$
P(t)=27+{\int }_{0}^{t}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $P$ is the number of bugs, and $t>0$ is the time (in days) since the observation started. 

At what time is the population of the colony a minimum, and what is the number of bugs at this time?

choices.value: The minimum is $16$ bugs after $2$ days
The minimum is $27$ bugs after $5$ days
The minimum is $11$ bugs after $2$ days
The minimum is $15$ bugs after $4$ days
The minimum is $8$ bugs after $4$ days

feedback.problem:
The total number of participants $S(t)$ registered for an online conference after $t$ days is given by the function

$$
S(t)=40+{\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in days, since the conference was announced. 

At what time is the number of participants at a minimum, and how many participants are registered at this time?
feedback.worked_solution:
To find when the number participants is minimized, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(40+{\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(40)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4t-16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=0$:

$$
4x-16=0\,⟹\,t=4
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=4.$ To find out how many participants are registered when $t=4,$ we figure out $S(4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}S(4) & =40+{\int }_{0}^{4}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x \\  & =40+{[2{x}^{2}-16x]|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =40+[(2(4)^{2}-16(4))-(0)] \\  & =40-32 \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Since $8<40$, we conclude that the minimum number of participants is $8$, and this occurs after $4$ days.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: The minimum is $8$ participants  after $4$ days
